newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnair chooses Airbus over Boeing for 12 planes.
newsitem.headline: Finnair chooses Airbus over Boeing for 12 planes.

text.p: Finnish national carrier Finnair Oy will buy 12 new aircraft from Airbus Industries, choosing the European plan maker over Boeing Co., the company said Friday.
Finnair said it would buy the Airbus 320-series and that its initial order for 12 aircraft would include an option for 24 more planes of the same series.
Finnair said it expected by pay about two billion markka, ($385 million), over a three-year period.
The exact value of the deal would be clear when Finnair decides which of the Airbus 320-series' three models -- the 126-seat A319, the 153-seat A320 and the 188-seat A321 -- it will buy.
Finnair said it expected to have the first two new planes -- both the A321 model -- in use at the start of 1999.
